title: Sub atomic particles
textbookText: These three categories are further divided as follows: Hadrons are composed of two or three quarks:
Baryons — protons, neutrons (each composed of three quarks) Mesons — pions, kaons (each composed of two quarks)
Baryons Mesons Leptons — electrons, muons, neutrinos — subject to the weak interaction. (Every particle has its own antiparticle.)
Leptons do not contain quarks. They themselves are considered to be fundamental particles.

26.3 Quarks Quarks were first proposed by two physicists working independently: Murray Gell-Mann and Georg Zweig . There are six different types or flavours of quarks. The six flavours are the up (u), charm (c) and top (t) quarks with electric charge 𝟐 𝒆, and the down (d), strange (s) and bottom (b) 𝟑 quarks with electric charge− 𝟏 𝒆. 𝟑 The top and bottom quarks are alternatively called truth and beauty. There is solid experimental evidence for the existence of all six flavours of quarks. In addition, we have the anti-particles of each of these. These have the same mass but all other properties are opposite, for example, electric charge. Anti-particles are denoted with a bar on top of the symbol for the name. We have already met two anti-particles: the anti-neutrino in beta minus decay, and the positron in beta plus decay. Quarks are never found as free particles. They are always combined together Particles composed of the combination of quarks are called hadrons. Hadrons are particles that experience both the weak and strong nuclear force. Quarks combine in just two ways to form hadrons.
